sanskrit: sanatsujāta uvāca yat tac chukraṃ mahaj jyotir dīpyamānaṃ mahad yaśaḥ tad vai devā upāsante yasmād arko virājate yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: Sanatsujata said: That radiant, supreme brilliance — that great light blazing, that great glory — the gods themselves worship it; from it the sun shines forth. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: śukrād brahma prabhavati brahma śukreṇa vardhate tac chukraṃ jyotiṣāṃ madhye 'taptaṃ tapati tāpanam yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: From that radiance Brahman is born; by that radiance Brahman grows. That radiance, in the midst of all lights, blazes without itself being heated, burning all others. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: āpo 'tha adbhyaḥ salilasya madhye; ubhau devau śiśriyāte 'ntarikṣe sa sadhrīcīḥ sa viṣūcīr vasānā; ubhe bibharti pṛthivīṃ divaṃ ca yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: The waters, then from the waters, in the midst of the flood — both deities dwell in the atmosphere; bearing united and diverse forms, he upholds both the earth and heaven. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: ubhau ca devau pṛthivīṃ divaṃ ca; diśaś ca śukraṃ bhuvanaṃ bibharti tasmād diśaḥ saritaś ca sravanti; tasmāt samudrā vihitā mahāntaḥ yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: Both deities — earth and heaven — and the directions: the radiant one upholds the entire universe. From him the directions and rivers flow; from him the great oceans are established. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: cakre rathasya tiṣṭhantaṃ dhruvasyāvyayakarmaṇaḥ ketumantaṃ vahanty aśvās taṃ divyam ajaraṃ divi yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: Dwelling at the hub of the wheel of the imperishable Dhruva — him who bears the banner, the horses carry that divine, ageless one in the sky. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: na sādṛśye tiṣṭhati rūpam asya; na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaś cid enam manīṣayātho manasā hṛdā ca; ya evaṃ vidur amṛtās te bhavanti yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: His form does not abide in any likeness; no one sees him with the eye. Through wisdom, through mind, and through the heart — those who know him thus become immortal. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: dvādaśapūgāṃ saritaṃ devarakṣitam madhu īśantas tadā saṃcaranti ghoram yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: Through the twelve-month stream guarded by the gods, the masters of honey move fearfully then. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: tad ardhamāsaṃ pibati saṃcitya bhramaro madhu īśānaḥ sarvabhūteṣu havirbhūtam akalpayat yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: The bee, having gathered it, drinks that honey for half a month; the Lord, who is oblation in all beings, ordained it so. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaparṇam aśvattham abhipatya apakṣakāḥ te tatra pakṣiṇo bhūtvā prapatanti yathādiśam yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: Having approached the golden-leafed Aśvattha tree, those without wings become birds there and fly off in their respective directions. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: pūrṇāt pūrṇāny uddharanti pūrṇāt pūrṇāni cakrire haranti pūrṇāt pūrṇāni pūrṇam evāvaśiṣyate yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: From the full, fullnesses are drawn; from the full, fullnesses are made and taken away; from the full, fullnesses arise — and yet fullness alone remains. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: tasmād vai vāyur āyātas tasmiṃś ca prayataḥ sadā tasmād agniś ca somaś ca tasmiṃś ca prāṇa ātataḥ
english: From him indeed the wind comes forth, and is ever reverently devoted to him; from him fire and soma arise, and in him the life-breath is extended.

sanskrit: sarvam eva tato vidyāt tat tad vaktuṃ na śaknumaḥ yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: One should know that all of this comes from him — yet all that cannot be spoken. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: apānaṃ girati prāṇaḥ prāṇaṃ girati candramāḥ ādityo girate candram ādityaṃ girate paraḥ yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: The out-breath swallows the in-breath; the moon swallows the in-breath; the sun swallows the moon; the Supreme swallows the sun. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: ekaṃ pādaṃ notkṣipati salilād dhaṃsa uccaran taṃ cet satatam ṛtvijaṃ na mṛtyur nāmṛtaṃ bhavet yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: The swan rising out of the water does not lift even one foot — if it were constantly worshipped as a priest, there would be neither death nor immortality. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: evaṃ devo mahātmā sa pāvakaṃ puruṣo giran yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ veda tasyehātmā na riṣyate yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: Thus that great-souled god, the Puruṣa, swallows the purifying fire; whoever truly knows that Puruṣa — his self is not destroyed here. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: yaḥ sahasraṃ sahasrāṇāṃ pakṣān saṃtatya saṃpatet madhyame madhya āgacched api cet syān manojavaḥ yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: One who were to spread a thousand thousand wings and fly, arriving at the very middle of the middle — even if swift as thought — the yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: na darśane tiṣṭhati rūpam asya; paśyanti cainaṃ suviśuddhasattvāḥ hito manīṣī manasābhipaśyed; ye taṃ śrayeyur amṛtās te bhavanti yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: His form does not abide in vision, yet those of perfectly pure nature see him. The wise, the benevolent, behold him with the mind; those who take refuge in him become immortal. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: gūhanti sarpā iva gahvarāṇi; svaśikṣayā svena vṛttena martyāḥ teṣu pramuhyanti janā vimūḍhā; yathādhvānaṃ mohayante bhayāya yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: As serpents hide in caverns, mortals hide behind their own learning and conduct; in them, confused people are deluded — just as one misleads travelers on a path to their fear. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: sadā sadāsatkṛtaḥ syān na mṛtyur amṛtaṃ kutaḥ satyānṛte satyasamānabandhane; sataś ca yonir asataś caika eva yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: One who is always treated as non-existent — there is no death for him, much less immortality. Truth and untruth, bound equally by truth; he is the sole womb of both the existent and the non-existent. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: na sādhunā nota asādhunā vā; samānam etad dṛśyate mānuṣeṣu samānam etad amṛtasya vidyād; evaṃyukto madhu tad vai parīpset yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: Neither by good deeds nor by evil — this is seen equally among humans; one should know this equally as the nectar of immortality. Thus united, one should seek that honey indeed. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: nāsyātivādā hṛdayaṃ tāpayanti; nānadhītaṃ nāhutam agnihotram mano brāhmīṃ laghutām ādadhīta; prajñānam asya nāma dhīrā labhante yoginas taṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam
english: Harsh words do not burn his heart; unlearned texts and unoffered fire-sacrifices do not trouble him. The mind should take on the lightness of Brahman; the wise attain the name of wisdom for him. The yogis behold him, the blessed, the eternal one.

sanskrit: evaṃ yaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ātmānam anupaśyati anyatrānyatra yukteṣu kiṃ sa śocet tataḥ param
english: One who thus sees the Self in all beings, and all beings engaged in various pursuits — what more should such a one grieve for?

sanskrit: yathodapāne mahati sarvataḥ saṃplutodake evaṃ sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
english: Just as in a great flood inundated everywhere a small well becomes superfluous, so are all the Vedas to a brahmin who truly knows.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo mahātmā; na dṛśyate 'sau hṛdaye niviṣṭaḥ ajaś caro divārātram atandritaś ca; sa taṃ matvā kavir āste prasannaḥ
english: The great-souled Puruṣa, the size of a thumb, dwelling in the heart, is not seen. Unborn, moving day and night, without fatigue — knowing him thus, the wise one abides in serenity.

sanskrit: aham evāsmi vo mātā pitā putro 'smy ahaṃ punaḥ ātmāham api sarvasya yac ca nāsti yad asti ca
english: I alone am your mother; I am your father; I am your son again. I am the Self of all — both what does not exist and what does exist.

sanskrit: pitāmaho 'smi sthaviraḥ pitā putraś ca bhārata mamaiva yūyam ātmasthā na me yūyaṃ na vo 'py aham
english: I am the aged grandfather, the father, and the son, O Bhārata. You all dwell in my Self — yet you are not mine, nor am I yours.

sanskrit: ātmaiva sthānaṃ mama janma cātmā; vedaprokto 'ham ajarapratiṣṭhaḥ
english: The Self alone is my abode; the Self is my birth. I am declared by the Vedas, established in the ageless one.

sanskrit: aṇor aṇīyān sumanāḥ sarvabhūteṣu jāgṛmi pitaraṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ puṣkare nihitaṃ viduḥ
english: Smaller than the smallest, well-disposed in mind, I watch over all beings. They know the father of all beings as placed in the lotus of the heart.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ sanatsujātena vidureṇa ca dhīmatā sārdhaṃ kathayato rājñaḥ sā vyatīyāya śarvarī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While Sanatsujata and the wise Vidura were thus conversing with the king, that night passed away.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ rājānaḥ sarva eva te sabhām āviviśur hṛṣṭāḥ sūtasyopadidṛkṣayā
english: When that night had passed, all those kings entered the assembly hall gladly, eager to see the charioteer's son.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣamāṇāḥ pārthānāṃ vaco dharmārthasaṃhitam dhṛtarāṣṭramukhāḥ sarve yayū rājasabhāṃ śubhām
english: Desiring to hear the message of the Pārthas — filled with righteousness and purpose — with Dhṛtarāṣṭra at their head, all went to the auspicious royal assembly.

sanskrit: sudhāvadātāṃ vistīrṇāṃ kanakājirabhūṣitām candraprabhāṃ surucirāṃ siktāṃ paramavāriṇā
english: The hall was white as plaster, vast, adorned with golden courtyards, radiant as the moon, most beautiful, sprinkled with the finest water.

sanskrit: rucirair āsanaiḥ stīrṇāṃ kāñcanair dāravair api aśmasāramayair dāntaiḥ svāstīrṇaiḥ sottaracchadaiḥ
english: Spread with beautiful seats — golden, wooden, made of the hardest stone, and of ivory — well-covered with upper coverings.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ śalyaḥ kṛtavarmā jayadrathaḥ aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca somadattaś ca bāhlikaḥ
english: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Śalya, Kṛtavarmā, Jayadratha, Aśvatthāmā, Vikarṇa, Somadatta, and Bāhlika —

sanskrit: viduraś ca mahāprājño yuyutsuś ca mahārathaḥ sarve ca sahitāḥ śūrāḥ pārthivā bharatarṣabha dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ puraskṛtya viviśus tāṃ sabhāṃ śubhām
english: And the greatly wise Vidura, and Yuyutsu the great warrior, and all those assembled heroes, the kings — placing Dhṛtarāṣṭra in front, they entered that auspicious assembly, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaś citrasenaḥ śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ durmukho duḥsahaḥ karṇa ulūko 'tha viviṃśatiḥ
english: Duḥśāsana, Citrasena, Śakuni the son of Subala, Durmukha, Duḥsaha, Karṇa, Ulūka, and Viviṃśati —

sanskrit: kururājaṃ puraskṛtya duryodhanam amarṣaṇam viviśus tāṃ sabhāṃ rājan surāḥ śakrasado yathā
english: Placing before them the Kuru king Duryodhana the intolerant, they entered that assembly, O king, like gods entering Indra's court.

sanskrit: āviśadbhis tadā rājañ śūraiḥ parighabāhubhiḥ śuśubhe sā sabhā rājan siṃhair iva girer guhā
english: As those heroes with arms like iron bars entered, O king, the assembly shone, O king, like a mountain cave filled with lions.

sanskrit: te praviśya maheṣvāsāḥ sabhāṃ samitiśobhanāḥ āsanāni mahārhāṇi bhejire sūryavarcasaḥ
english: Those great archers, splendid in assembly, having entered, took their places on the most worthy seats, resplendent as the sun.

sanskrit: āsanastheṣu sarveṣu teṣu rājasu bhārata dvāḥstho nivedayām āsa sūtaputram upasthitam
english: When all those kings were seated on their thrones, O Bhārata, the doorkeeper announced that the charioteer's son had arrived.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa ratha āyāti yo 'yāsīt pāṇḍavān prati dūto nas tūrṇam āyātaḥ saindhavaiḥ sādhuvāhibhiḥ
english: That chariot comes which went to the Pāṇḍavas on our behalf; the envoy has returned quickly, drawn by excellent Sindhu horses.

sanskrit: upayāya tu sa kṣipraṃ rathāt praskandya kuṇḍalī praviveśa sabhāṃ pūrṇāṃ mahīpālair mahātmabhiḥ
english: Having come near, he quickly leapt from the chariot — wearing his earrings — and entered the full assembly thronged with great-souled kings.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prāpto 'smi pāṇḍavān gatvā tad vijānīta kauravāḥ yathāvayaḥ kurūn sarvān pratinandanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Sañjaya said: I have returned from going to the Pāṇḍavas — know this, O Kauravas. The Pāṇḍavas greet all the Kurus according to their age.

sanskrit: abhivādayanti vṛddhāṃś ca vayasyāṃś ca vayasyavat yūnaś cābhyavadan pārthāḥ pratipūjya yathāvayaḥ
english: They bow to the elders and treat equals as equals; the sons of Pṛthā addressed the young ones, honouring each according to age.

sanskrit: yathāhaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa śiṣṭaḥ pūrvam ito gataḥ abruvaṃ pāṇḍavān gatvā tan nibodhata pārthivāḥ
english: As I was instructed by Dhṛtarāṣṭra when I departed hence, so I spoke to the Pāṇḍavas when I went. Hear that, O kings.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca pṛcchāmi tvāṃ saṃjaya rājamadhye; kim abravīd vākyam adīnasattvaḥ dhanaṃjayas tāta yudhāṃ praṇetā; durātmanāṃ jīvitacchin mahātmā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: I ask you, Sañjaya, in the midst of the kings — what did the great-spirited Dhanañjaya say, dear one? He is the leader of warriors, the cutter of the lives of the wicked, the great-souled one.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca duryodhano vācam imāṃ śṛṇotu; yad abravīd arjuno yotsyamānaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasyānumate mahātmā; dhanaṃjayaḥ śṛṇvataḥ keśavasya
english: Sañjaya said: Let Duryodhana hear these words that Arjuna, preparing to fight, the great-souled one with Yudhiṣṭhira's approval, spoke — Dhanañjaya, while Keśava listened.

sanskrit: anvatrasto bāhuvīryaṃ vidāna; upahvare vāsudevasya dhīraḥ avocan māṃ yotsyamānaḥ kirīṭī; madhye brūyā dhārtarāṣṭraṃ kurūṇām
english: Knowing his own arm-strength, unafraid, the steady one, in private with Vāsudeva, Kirīṭī spoke to me while preparing for battle: 'Speak this in the midst of the Kurus to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.'

sanskrit: ye vai rājānaḥ pāṇḍavāyodhanāya; samānītāḥ śṛṇvatāṃ cāpi teṣām yathā samagraṃ vacanaṃ mayoktaṃ; sahāmātyaṃ śrāvayethā nṛpaṃ tam
english: All the kings who have been assembled for battle against the Pāṇḍavas, let them also hear: exactly as I spoke my complete message, convey it to that king along with his ministers.

sanskrit: yathā nūnaṃ devarājasya devāḥ; śuśrūṣante vajrahastasya sarve tathāśṛṇvan pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayāś ca; kirīṭinā vācam uktāṃ samarthām
english: Just as all the gods attend upon the king of gods, the thunderbolt-armed Indra, so the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas listened to the well-reasoned words spoken by the diademed one.

sanskrit: ity abravīd arjuno yotsyamāno; gāṇḍīvadhanvā lohitapadmanetraḥ na ced rājyaṃ muñcati dhārtarāṣṭro; yudhiṣṭhirasyājamīḍhasya rājñaḥ asti nūnaṃ karma kṛtaṃ purastād; anirviṣṭaṃ pāpakaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraiḥ
english: Thus spoke Arjuna, the Gāṇḍīva-bowman with eyes like red lotuses, preparing for battle: 'If the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra does not release the kingdom of Yudhiṣṭhira — king of the Ajamīḍha line — then there is indeed some evil deed committed before by the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra that has not yet been expiated.'

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ yuddhaṃ bhīmasenārjunābhyāṃ; tathāśvibhyāṃ vāsudevena caiva śaineyena dhruvam āttāyudhena; dhṛṣṭadyumnenātha śikhaṇḍinā ca yudhiṣṭhireṇendrakalpena caiva; yo 'padhyānān nirdahed gāṃ divaṃ ca
english: Those who face battle with Bhīmasena and Arjuna, with the twin Aśvins, with Vāsudeva, with Saineya surely weapon in hand, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍī, and with Yudhiṣṭhira who is like Indra himself — who could burn earth and heaven with his very wrath —

sanskrit: taiś ced yuddhaṃ manyate dhārtarāṣṭro; nirvṛtto 'rthaḥ sakalaḥ pāṇḍavānām mā tat kārṣīḥ pāṇḍavārthāya hetor; upaihi yuddhaṃ yadi manyase tvam
english: If the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra thinks he should fight with them, the entire aim of the Pāṇḍavas is accomplished. Do not do that for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas' cause; but if you think so, then come to battle.

sanskrit: yāṃ tāṃ vane duḥkhaśayyām uvāsa; pravrājitaḥ pāṇḍavo dharmacārī āśiṣyate duḥkhatarām anarthām; antyāṃ śayyāṃ dhārtarāṣṭraḥ parāsuḥ
english: The Pāṇḍava who follows dharma and was sent into exile — the hard bed on which he lay in the forest — the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will meet with a far worse, miserable, and disastrous final bed, bereft of life.

sanskrit: hriyā jñānena tapasā damena; krodhenātho dharmaguptyā dhanena anyāyavṛttaḥ kurupāṇḍaveyān; adhyātiṣṭhad dhārtarāṣṭro durātmā
english: With modesty, knowledge, austerity, and self-restraint, with wrath, with protection of dharma and with wealth — acting wrongfully, the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra has been lording it over the Kuru Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: māyopadhaḥ praṇidhānārjavābhyāṃ; tapodamābhyāṃ dharmaguptyā balena satyaṃ bruvan prītiyuktyānṛtena; titikṣamāṇaḥ kliśyamāno 'tivelam
english: Deceitful in foundation, with spies and with straightforwardness, with austerity and self-control, with protection of dharma and strength, speaking truth yet joining lies with affection, forbearing and suffering excessively long —

sanskrit: yadā jyeṣṭhaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ saṃśitātmā; krodhaṃ yat taṃ varṣapūgān sughoram avasraṣṭā kuruṣūdvṛttacetās; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When the eldest Pāṇḍava of disciplined soul, his mind provoked to excess among the Kurus, shall release that terrible wrath long restrained through many years — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇavartmeva jvalitaḥ samiddho; yathā dahet kakṣam agnir nidāghe evaṃ dagdhā dhārtarāṣṭrasya senāṃ; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ krodhadīpto 'nuvīkṣya
english: Blazing like a fire with a black trail when fully kindled, as fire would burn dry grass in summer — so Yudhiṣṭhira, blazing with wrath, will burn the army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son upon encountering it.

sanskrit: yadā draṣṭā bhīmasenaṃ raṇasthaṃ; gadāhastaṃ krodhaviṣaṃ vamantam durmarṣaṇaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ bhīmavegaṃ; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When he shall see Bhīmasena standing on the battlefield, mace in hand, vomiting the poison of his wrath, that intolerant Pāṇḍava of terrible speed — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: mahāsiṃho gāva iva praviśya; gadāpāṇir dhārtarāṣṭrān upetya yadā bhīmo bhīmarūpo nihantā; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: Like a great lion entering among cattle, mace in hand, approaching the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — when Bhīma of terrible form becomes the slayer — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: mahābhaye vītabhayaḥ kṛtāstraḥ; samāgame śatrubalāvamardī sakṛd rathena pratiyād rathaughān; padātisaṃghān gadayābhinighnan
english: Fearless in great fear, accomplished in arms, a crusher of enemy forces in combat — at once charging the masses of chariots with his chariot, striking down crowds of foot-soldiers with his mace —

sanskrit: sainyān anekāṃs tarasā vimṛdnan; yadā kṣeptā dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainyam chindan vanaṃ paraśuneva śūras; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: Swiftly crushing many soldiers, when he hurls himself to scatter the army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, cutting like a hero with an axe through a forest — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: tṛṇaprāyaṃ jvalaneneva dagdhaṃ; grāmaṃ yathā dhārtarāṣṭraḥ samīkṣya pakvaṃ sasyaṃ vaidyuteneva dagdhaṃ; parāsiktaṃ vipulaṃ svaṃ balaugham
english: When the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra beholds his own vast host of soldiers scattered and deluged — like a village burned by fire as though mere grass, like a ripe crop burned by lightning —

sanskrit: hatapravīraṃ vimukhaṃ bhayārtaṃ; parāṅmukhaṃ prāyaśo 'dhṛṣṭayodham śastrārciṣā bhīmasenena dagdhaṃ; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: Its heroes slain, turning away, seized with fear, mostly with backs turned, its warriors mostly daunted, burned by the flame of Bhīmasena's weapons — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: upāsaṅgād uddharan dakṣiṇena; paraḥśatān nakulaś citrayodhī yadā rathāgryo rathinaḥ pracetā; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When Nakula the skillful warrior, drawing from his quiver with his right hand, slaying hundreds — the foremost of chariot fighters, the knowing warrior — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: sukhocito duḥkhaśayyāṃ vaneṣu; dīrghaṃ kālaṃ nakulo yām aśeta āśīviṣaḥ kruddha iva śvasan bhṛśaṃ; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When Nakula — accustomed to comfort but who long lay on the hard bed of the forests — hisses greatly like an enraged venomous serpent — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: tyaktātmānaḥ pārthivāyodhanāya; samādiṣṭā dharmarājena vīrāḥ rathaiḥ śubhraiḥ sainyam abhidravanto; dṛṣṭvā paścāt tapsyate dhārtarāṣṭraḥ
english: Heroes who have given up their lives for battle with the kings, commanded by Dharmarāja, charging the army with gleaming chariots — seeing them, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will afterwards repent.

sanskrit: śiśūn kṛtāstrān aśiśuprakāśān; yadā draṣṭā kauravaḥ pañca śūrān tyaktvā prāṇān kekayān ādravantas; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When the Kaurava shall see those five young heroes accomplished in arms yet not appearing as mere children, the Kekayas charging with lives renounced — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: yadā gatodvāham akūjanākṣaṃ; suvarṇatāraṃ ratham ātatāyī dāntair yuktaṃ sahadevo 'dhirūḍhaḥ; śirāṃsi rājñāṃ kṣepsyate mārgaṇaughaiḥ
english: When the relentless one, Sahadeva, mounts the chariot whose wheels move silently, with golden stars, yoked with ivory-white horses, and will hurl off the heads of kings with streams of arrows —

sanskrit: mahābhaye saṃpravṛtte rathasthaṃ; vivartamānaṃ samare kṛtāstram sarvāṃ diśaṃ saṃpatantaṃ samīkṣya; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When a great terror erupts, beholding him standing on his chariot, whirling in battle, accomplished in arms, flying out in every direction — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: hrīniṣedho nipuṇaḥ satyavādī; mahābalaḥ sarvadharmopapannaḥ gāndhārim ārcchaṃs tumule kṣiprakārī; kṣeptā janān sahadevas tarasvī
english: He who restrains by shame, subtle, truth-speaking, of great strength, endowed with all dharmas — Sahadeva the swift-acting, the swift one, hurling men, striking in the tumult towards Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: yadā draṣṭā draupadeyān maheṣūñ; śūrān kṛtāstrān rathayuddhakovidān āśīviṣān ghoraviṣān ivāyatas; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When he shall see the mighty archers, the sons of Draupadī, heroes skilled in arms, expert in chariot warfare, approaching like venomous serpents of terrible venom — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: yadābhimanyuḥ paravīraghātī; śaraiḥ parān megha ivābhivarṣan vigāhitā kṛṣṇasamaḥ kṛtāstras; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When Abhimanyu, slayer of enemy heroes, raining down arrows on foes like a cloud, plunging deep into battle, equal to Kṛṣṇa in arms — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: yadā draṣṭā bālam abālavīryaṃ; dviṣaccamūṃ mṛtyum ivāpatantam saubhadram indrapratimaṃ kṛtāstraṃ; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When he shall see the boy of no boyish valor, Subhadrā's son, equal to Indra in arms, falling upon the enemy army like death itself — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: prabhadrakāḥ śīghratarā yuvāno; viśāradāḥ siṃhasamānavīryāḥ yadā kṣeptāro dhārtarāṣṭrān sasainyāṃs; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: The Prabhadrakas — swifter than swift, young, skilled, of lion-like valor — when they are the ones hurling themselves upon the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra with their armies — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: vṛddhau virāṭadrupadau mahārathau; pṛthak camūbhyām abhivartamānau yadā draṣṭārau dhārtarāṣṭrān sasainyāṃs; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When he shall see the two aged great warriors Virāṭa and Drupada, each advancing with his own division against the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and their armies — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: yadā kṛtāstro drupadaḥ pracinvañ; śirāṃsi yūnāṃ samare rathasthaḥ kruddhaḥ śaraiś chetsyati cāpamuktais; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When Drupada, accomplished in arms, shall cut off the heads of young warriors in battle, standing on his chariot, in his wrath, with arrows released from his bow — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: yadā virāṭaḥ paravīraghātī; marmāntare śatrucamūṃ praveṣṭā matsyaiḥ sārdham anṛśaṃsarūpais; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When Virāṭa the slayer of enemy heroes shall pierce into the vitals of the enemy host together with the Matsyas of fierce appearance — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaṃ mātsyānām anṛśaṃsarūpaṃ; virāṭaputraṃ rathinaṃ purastāt yadā draṣṭā daṃśitaṃ pāṇḍavārthe; tadā yuddhaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro 'nvatapsyat
english: When he shall see the eldest of the Matsyas, of fierce appearance, the son of Virāṭa, a chariot warrior, armored and deployed at the front for the cause of the Pāṇḍavas — then the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will repent of battle.

sanskrit: raṇe hate kauravāṇāṃ pravīre; śikhaṇḍinā sattame śaṃtanūje na jātu naḥ śatravo dhārayeyur; asaṃśayaṃ satyam etad bravīmi
english: When the foremost hero of the Kauravas — the best of Shantanu's sons — is slain in battle by Śikhaṇḍī, our enemies will never be able to hold out. I declare this without doubt, as truth.
